name: Ahmad ibn Fadlan
summary: Secretary to the Abbasid caliph's embassy to the king of the Volga Bulghars, he crosses Iran, Khwarazm and the steppe in winter and describes the Oghuz, Bashkirs and a Rus ship funeral.

stops.note: Leaves with the envoy Susan al-Rassi carrying the caliph al-Muqtadir's letter and gifts.
Crosses the Zagros on the Khurasan road.
Waits several days because the Daylamite ruler controls the road.
Continues to the Oxus crossing at Amul.
Meets the young Samanid emir Nasr ibn Ahmad; the promised money to fund the mission is not ready.
Winters in Khwarazm in bitter cold; camels' beards freeze.
Climbs onto the plateau in deep snow with a caravan of 3,000 horses and 5,000 men.
Negotiates passage with the Oghuz army commander.
Crosses the river in camel-skin boats; meets Pechenegs.
Fears the Bashkirs, whom he calls the most dangerous of the Turks.
Reads the caliph's letter to the Bulghar king Almish and is blamed for the missing money.
Witnesses the Rus merchants and the ship funeral of a chieftain.

sources.cite: Ibn Fadlan, Mission to the Volga, trans. James E. Montgomery, in Two Arabic Travel Books, New York University Press 2014
Ibn Fadlan and the Land of Darkness, trans. Paul Lunde and Caroline Stone, Penguin 2012
